privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.body:
Last updated: 29 October 2026

Route Forge is an app for courier firms. Couriers record their shifts, dispatchers review them, and the firm's owner sees hours and pay. This policy explains which personal data the app processes, why, where it is stored and what your rights are.

# 1. Who is responsible

Your firm (the company you work or drive for) decides which data it needs for shifts and pay and is the controller of that data. Route Forge processes it on your firm's behalf. Route Forge is operated by Nikolay Gospodinov, Halmhuberstraße 4, 68219 Mannheim-Rheinau, Germany. Contact: support@routeforge.app.

# 2. Which data

• Account: your name and email address; if you sign in with Google, the name and email of your Google account. Passwords are kept only by our sign-in provider, never in readable form.
• Your role in the firm and, for dispatchers, their depots.
• Shifts: date, start and finish time, depot, car, kilometres, packages loaded, returned and picked up, and the review (approved or rejected, corrections with who made them and when).
• Pay: your pay rate, and the hours, pay and Spesen calculated from your approved shifts.
• Vehicle check photos you take of the car, logbook, Mentor score and fuel gauges.
• Documents you choose to add, with their photos: ID card, driving licence, registered address, tax ID and tax class, social security number, health insurance, certificate of good conduct (Führungszeugnis), bank account and contacts. All of them are optional.
• Service log notes and their photos, written by mechanics and owners.
• Crash reports: device model, operating system, app version and what went wrong, without your name, email or other personal details.

Route Forge has no advertising, tracking or analytics, and never sells data.

# 3. Why, and on what legal basis

The data is used to record working time, review shifts, calculate pay and keep the firm's cars roadworthy. The legal basis is your employment or service contract with your firm (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR), your firm's legal duty to record working time and keep payroll records (Art. 6(1)(c) GDPR), and, for crash reports, the legitimate interest in an app that works (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).

# 4. Who can see it

• You see your own shifts, pay, rate and documents.
• Your firm's owner sees everything in the firm, including pay and documents.
• Dispatchers see shifts, their photos and their pay in their own depots, never your documents.
• Mechanics see car papers, service log notes, and vehicle check photos of the last 7 days with your name only.
• No other firm can see your data.

# 5. Service providers and where data is stored

• Clerk (Clerk, Inc., USA): sign-in and accounts.
• Neon (USA): the database, hosted in Frankfurt, Germany.
• Cloudflare (Cloudflare, Inc., USA): photos and documents, stored in the EU; email forwarding for support.
• Expo (650 Industries, Inc., USA): hosting of the app's server.
• Sentry (Functional Software, Inc., USA): crash reports, stored in Germany.
• Google: only if you choose to sign in with Google.

These providers process data only on instructions and under data processing agreements. Where data reaches the USA, the transfer is covered by the EU–US Data Privacy Framework or the EU Standard Contractual Clauses.

# 6. How long data is kept

• Vehicle check photos: deleted automatically 14 days after they're taken.
• Uploads that were started but never saved: deleted after one day.
• Documents and their photos: until you or your firm's owner remove them, or you delete your account.
• Shifts, pay and service log notes: kept by your firm as long as payroll and tax law require (in Germany up to 10 years), also after you leave or delete your account.
• Your login: until you delete your account or your firm removes you.
• Crash reports: up to 90 days.

# 7. Deleting your account

In the app: Profile → Delete account. Your login, your documents and their photos are deleted at once. Your shifts, pay, service log notes and any vehicle check photos still within their 14 days stay with your firm, which must keep them by law, and show as "Deleted user". Firm owners write to support@routeforge.app. Step by step: route-forge.expo.app/delete-account.

# 8. Your rights

You have the right to access your data, to have it corrected or deleted, to restrict or object to its processing, and to receive it in a portable format. For shift and pay data, contact your firm first, as it is the controller; you can also write to support@routeforge.app, and we will help or pass your request on. You can complain to a data protection supervisory authority, for example the one where you live or work.

# 9. Security

Data is encrypted in transit and at rest. Photos and documents are never public: they open only through links that expire after an hour. Each firm's data is kept apart from every other firm's.

# 10. Age

Route Forge is a work app and is not meant for anyone under 18.

# 11. Changes

When this policy changes, the new version is published here with a new date.

deleteAccount.title: Delete your account
deleteAccount.body:
1. Open Route Forge and sign in.

2. Go to Profile and tap Delete account at the bottom.

3. Confirm with Delete my account.

What's deleted: your login, your documents and their photos. What stays with your firm: your shifts, vehicle check photos (deleted 14 days after they're taken), service log notes and pay, which the firm must keep by law.

Firm owners can't delete their account in the app. Contact Route Forge support at support@routeforge.app.
